## Dataset API Overview

`fmrimod.dataset` is where dataset containers and storage adapters live.
Import them from `fmrimod` or `fmrimod.dataset`. (If you are reading
older code that imports `fmridataset`, that name still works as a
re-export; see the migration note at the end.)

A dataset's job is to bind your data to its timing and events so every
later step reads them from one place instead of re-deriving them. A
typical workflow is:

```text
matrix_dataset / fmri_dataset
  -> fmri_lm or single-trial estimator
  -> contrasts
  -> group_data or group_fit
```

Use these entry points as the public surface:

| Need | Use | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Timing grid | `SamplingFrame` | Shared by design and dataset code. |
| In-memory matrices | `matrix_dataset()` | Tests, simulations, and pre-extracted features. |
| Image-backed data | `fmri_dataset()` | Real image IO should enter through the neuroim-compatible boundary. |
| Low-rank features | `latent_dataset()` | Stores component scores with optional loadings. |
| Study tables | `study_dataset()` / `fmri_group()` | Subject-level containers feeding native group analysis. |
| Chunked voxel work | `data_chunks()` / `voxel_index_chunks()` | Batch execution without changing the model contract. |
| BIDS-HDF5 archives | `bids_h5_dataset()` / `compress_bids_study()` | Optional HDF5/BIDS IO boundary, not a second tutorial track. |

## Sampling Frames

`SamplingFrame` describes the acquired time grid, including run lengths. In
the canonical dataset contract, `samples` are acquisition times in seconds.

::: {#f602d4c1 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import neuroim as ni
import fmrimod as fm

sf = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=[50, 50], TR=2.0)
sf.samples[:6], sf.blocklens
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1}
```
(array([ 1.,  3.,  5.,  7.,  9., 11.]), array([50, 50]))
```
:::
:::


## Matrix Data

Use `matrix_dataset()` when data already live in memory as a time by voxel
matrix. Real image-backed workflows should route through the dataset adapters
and, ultimately, neuroim-python containers at the image boundary.

::: {#4702f0b7 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
rng = np.random.default_rng(11)
events = pd.DataFrame({
    "run": [1, 1, 2, 2],
    "onset": [10, 30, 12, 32],
    "condition": ["face", "scene", "face", "scene"],
})

data = rng.normal(size=(100, 20))
dset = fm.matrix_dataset(
    data,
    tr=2.0,
    run_length=[50, 50],
    event_table=events,
)

dset
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
FmriDataset(n_runs=2, n_timepoints=100, n_voxels=20)
```
:::
:::


::: {#c6d4b145 .cell execution_count=3}
``` {.python .cell-code}
dset.n_runs, dset.n_timepoints, dset.n_voxels
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3}
```
(2, 100, 20)
```
:::
:::


::: {#6a9cf9bf .cell execution_count=4}
``` {.python .cell-code}
dset.get_data(rows=[0, 1, 2], cols=[0, 1]).shape, dset.get_all_data().shape
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4}
```
((3, 2), (100, 20))
```
:::
:::


## Image and Archive IO

`fmri_dataset()` is the preferred constructor when a workflow starts from
image-like objects or paths. It keeps image IO at the boundary and returns the
same typed `FmriDataset` object used by matrix-backed examples.

Here is the same two-run shape using neuroim objects. The example stays small
and network-free, but it exercises the real spatial adapter: each run is a
`DenseNeuroVec`, the mask is a `LogicalNeuroVol`, and one dataset owns both
runs.

::: {#9f77d536 .cell execution_count=5}
``` {.python .cell-code}
spatial_shape = (5, 4, 3)
image_affine = np.array([
    [-2.0, 0.0, 0.0, 8.0],
    [0.0, 2.5, 0.0, -6.0],
    [0.0, 0.0, 3.0, 4.0],
    [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
])

mask_array = np.zeros(spatial_shape, dtype=bool)
mask_array[1:4, 1:3, :] = True
mask_vol = ni.LogicalNeuroVol(
    mask_array,
    ni.NeuroSpace.from_affine(image_affine, spatial_shape),
)

image_run_lengths = (12, 10)
run_vecs = tuple(
    ni.DenseNeuroVec(
        np.random.default_rng(seed).normal(
            size=spatial_shape + (n_time,)
        ),
        ni.NeuroSpace.from_affine(
            image_affine,
            spatial_shape + (n_time,),
        ),
    )
    for seed, n_time in zip((21, 22), image_run_lengths, strict=True)
)

image_events = pd.DataFrame({
    "run": [1, 2],
    "onset": [2.0, 4.0],
    "duration": [1.0, 1.0],
    "condition": ["face", "scene"],
})
image_dset = fm.fmri_dataset(
    run_vecs,
    mask=mask_vol,
    tr=2.0,
    events=image_events,
)

pd.Series({
    "dataset": type(image_dset).__name__,
    "image object": type(run_vecs[0]).__name__,
    "mask object": type(mask_vol).__name__,
    "runs": image_dset.n_runs,
    "run lengths": tuple(image_dset.run_lengths),
    "mask shape": image_dset.get_mask().shape,
    "masked voxels": image_dset.n_voxels,
})
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5}
```
dataset              FmriDataset
image object       DenseNeuroVec
mask object      LogicalNeuroVol
runs                           2
run lengths             (12, 10)
mask shape             (5, 4, 3)
masked voxels                 18
dtype: object
```
:::
:::


The adapter performs the image-to-matrix boundary when a model asks for one
run's data. The `NeuroVec` and `NeuroVol` retain the signed affine; downstream
contrast and export objects use that retained spatial context to return results
to the same grid. There is no user-managed flattening or identity affine.

BIDS-HDF5 helpers are available when a workflow needs a compact archive:

- `compress_bids_study()` writes a v1 BIDS-HDF5 archive from already
  materialized datasets, or from an optional BIDS-directory IO path when the
  BIDS/NIfTI dependencies are installed.
- `bids_h5_dataset()` opens the archive as a study object whose scan backends
  follow the same feature-space storage contract as matrix, latent, HDF5, and
  NIfTI-backed datasets.

Use these when you need a single compact, shareable archive for a study;
for everyday in-memory work the matrix and image constructors above are
all you need.

## Latent Data

Latent datasets store component scores and optional loadings. They can be used
when the time series has been compressed before modeling.

::: {#c351a1eb .cell execution_count=6}
``` {.python .cell-code}
scores = rng.normal(size=(100, 4))
loadings = rng.normal(size=(4, 20))

latent = fm.latent_dataset(
    scores,
    loadings=loadings,
    tr=2.0,
    run_length=[50, 50],
    event_table=events,
)

latent.n_runs, latent.n_voxels, latent.get_scores(0).shape
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6}
```
(2, 20, (50, 4))
```
:::
:::


## Chunking

Chunk helpers make it easy to split voxel-space work into reviewable batches.
`data_chunks()` yields typed `DataChunk` objects carrying data and indices;
`voxel_index_chunks()` is the legacy index-only helper.

::: {#c9a4f06c .cell execution_count=7}
``` {.python .cell-code}
chunks = fm.data_chunks(dset, nchunks=4)
[(chunk.chunk_num, chunk.data.shape, chunk.voxel_ind.tolist()) for chunk in chunks]
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=7}
```
[(1, (100, 5), [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]),
 (2, (100, 5), [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]),
 (3, (100, 5), [10, 11, 12, 13, 14]),
 (4, (100, 5), [15, 16, 17, 18, 19])]
```
:::
:::


## Migrating From fmridataset

If you have code that imports `fmridataset`, change the import to
`fmrimod.dataset` (or `fmrimod`). The objects are the same, so this is
a find-and-replace, not a rewrite. The re-export returns the identical
class object. The historical `fmridataset` distribution is not a docs
dependency, so this compatibility check is shown but deliberately not run in
the site build:

<!-- docs-nonexecuted: optional historical fmridataset package is not a docs dependency -->

::: {#9f231833 .cell execution_count=8}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import fmridataset
import fmrimod.dataset as ds

fmridataset.FmriDataset is ds.FmriDataset
```
:::


If a name you used under `fmridataset` is not available, it has not been
ported yet. There are no stub placeholders, so an `ImportError` here
means "not yet", not "moved somewhere subtle".
